lines: Title: Some users may see delays receiving policies, apps, and other changes on Windows devices enrolled in Microsoft Intune
User impact: Users may see delays receiving policies, apps, and other changes on Windows devices enrolled in Microsoft Intune.

More info: A recent Windows security update, MSRC144654, can cause a single device check in to fail during installation. Affected devices receive pending changes at their next successful check in. Users can check in manually after the update finishes instead of waiting for the next scheduled check in.

Current status: We anticipate that our fix will be available by our next scheduled communication. We'll continue to monitor deployment and provide any updates to this remediation timeline as soon as they become available.

Scope of impact: Some users with Windows devices enrolled in Microsoft Intune may experience delays receiving policies, apps, and other changes while their devices install Windows security update MSRC144654. This information may be updated as our investigation continues.

Root cause: A recent Windows security update, MSRC144654, can cause a single check in to fail during installation.

lines: Title: Some users may be unable to view organization information in multiple Microsoft 365 services
User impact: Users may be unable to view organization information in multiple Microsoft 365 services.
More info: Affected users report that Organization Explorer appears empty or doesn't display the expected organizational information in Microsoft Teams, Outlook desktop client and Outlook on the web.

Current status: We've identified two potential mitigation options and are determining which will be the safest and most effective. We'll provide additional information on the resolution timeline based on the results of our analysis by our next scheduled communications update.

Scope of impact: This issue may affect some users who are attempting to view organization information in multiple Microsoft 365 services are impacted. This section may be updated as our investigation progresses.
Root cause: One code path for processes that refresh cached user data causes the data to not be returned as expected, resulting in an incorrect evaluation of the user's organizational relationship.

lines: Title: Admins can't identify who deleted a Viva Engage community or its Microsoft 365 Group in Microsoft Entra ID audit logs
User impact: Admins couldn't identify who deleted a Viva Engage community or its Microsoft 365 Group in Entra ID audit logs.
More info: Impact applied to deletions initiated from both the Viva Engage web experience and the Viva Engage app in Microsoft Teams.

Admins who needed to identify who deleted a specific community or group during the affected period could have opened a Microsoft support case with the deletion date and group/community details so support could trace the initiating user through service-side logs.

Final status: After identifying additional options to expedite remediation, we've confirmed that all three phases of our fix have deployed earlier than expected. We've validated its efficacy and ensured that users who delete Viva Engage or Microsoft 365 groups are now logged in Microsoft Entra ID audit logs.
Scope of impact: This issue prevented all admins from identifying who deleted Viva Engage communities or their connected Microsoft 365 Group in Microsoft Entra ID audit logs.
Start time: Friday, July 10, 2026, at 2:05 PM UTC
End time: Wednesday, October 21, 2026, at 4:30 PM UTC
Root cause: A recent update to improve group deletions of Viva Engage communities within Microsoft Teams resulted in impact.
Next steps:
- We're continuing to consult user reports to identify problem-causing scenarios so that we can develop comprehensive feature changes that meet user needs.
This is the final update for the event.

lines: Title: Some users may be missing the "Meeting options" button for Microsoft Teams meetings in multiple Microsoft 365 apps
User impact: Users may have been missing the "Meeting options" button for Microsoft Teams meetings in multiple Microsoft 365 apps.
More info: This issue was occurring in the following Microsoft 365 apps:
- Microsoft Teams desktop client
- Microsoft Teams web client
- Outlook on the web
- Outlook desktop client
The issue only occurred in standard Teams meetings, and live events, webinars, and town halls weren’t affected.
Final status: We've validated with a subset of affected users that our rollback of the problematic tenant filter has remediated impact.
Scope of impact: This issue impacted some users who may have been missing the "Meeting options” button when creating standard meetings using multiple Microsoft 365 apps.
Start time: Monday, October 12, 2026, at 8:48 PM UTC
End time: Wednesday, October 14, 2026, at 6:16 PM UTC
Root cause: A tenant filter to disable the "Meeting options" button for a specific organization was unintentionally applied broadly to multiple organizations.
Next steps:

- We're analyzing the problematic tenant filter to validate why it was applied broadly to further our understanding of how the issue was introduced and to evaluate what actions we can take to prevent similar impact scenarios from occurring in the future.
This is the final update for the event.

Title: Some users may have been unable to open or upload attachments in the new Outlook client
User impact: Users may have been to open or upload attachments or view inline images in the new Outlook client.
More info: Affected users may have been able to use Outlook on the web or the Outlook classic client to open or upload attachments and view inline images.

Final status: The supplemental fix has successfully saturated across the remaining affected environments. We’ve monitored the service following the deployment and confirmed that impact has been remediated.

Users who are actively using the new Outlook client and continue to experience impact may need to close and reopen the client for the fix to take effect. Otherwise, the fix will be applied automatically the next time users open the new Outlook client.
Scope of impact: Some users attempting to open or upload attachments or view inline images in email messages may have been impacted.
Start time: Thursday, November 19, 2026, at 8:49 PM UTC
End time: Saturday, November 21, 2026, at 8:25 AM UTC

Root cause: We determined that a recent update to the code path that supports embedded web content introduced additional metadata validation for handle access. Some existing handles did not include the new metadata, which caused affected attachment operations in the new Outlook client to hang when those handles were accessed. This condition led to failures when users attempted to open or upload attachments and, for some users, to view inline images. We developed and deployed supplemental fixes, then continued monitored saturation across environments to restore consistent behaviour.
- For a more comprehensive list of next steps and actions, please refer to the Post Incident Report document.

lines: Title: Some users may be unable to send calendar invitations in Exchange Online
User impact: Users may have been unable to send calendar invitations in Exchange Online.
More info: Users may have been unable to send calendar invitations due to hitting an incorrect recipient limit of 25 users for affected messages.

Final status: Following the initiating of our aforementioned fix across the affected environment, we’ve confirmed with a subset of users and our monitoring telemetry that impact has been fully resolved.
Scope of impact: This issue may have impacted some users who attempted to send calendar invitations in Exchange Online due to hitting a recipient limit of 25 users.
Start time: Tuesday, November 10, 2026, at 12:00 AM UTC
End time: Thursday, November 26, 2026, at 11:30 PM UTC
Root cause: A recent service update removed the "MeetingMessage" traffic subtype from affected messages, which caused a lower recipient limit of 25 to be applied instead of the standard 5000.

Next steps: - We’re continuing to analyze why the recent service update removed the "MeetingMessage" traffic subtype from affected messages to determine why the potential for impact wasn't caught during the update testing and validation phase. These actions will help us to clarify what actions we can take to ensure that similar impact doesn't occur in the future and to continue our ongoing mission to improve the resilience of our service for all Exchange Online users.
This is the final update for this event.

lines: Title: Users may be unable to view contacts and Speed Dial entries in Microsoft Teams, Outlook desktop and mobile
User impact: Users may have been unable to view contacts and Speed Dial entries in Microsoft Teams, Outlook desktop and mobile.

More info: Affected users may have observed missing contacts, blank or grey placeholder entries, or Speed Dial entries that couldn't be re-added. This behavior may have occurred across Microsoft Teams desktop and web experiences, Outlook Mobile, and Outlook desktop.

More specifically, this issue impacted in-tenant contacts created in Microsoft Teams using the Notify when available presence notification option. Some older contacts may also have been impacted under specific circumstances.

Final status: We’ve completed deployment of the code fix to repair the remaining affected contacts on a user basis and confirmed that impact is remediated. Some contacts may still be blank; however, we're unable to automate a fix to resolve all instances of blank contacts. We recommend users to delete the blank contacts and add them again. If they add a contact from a profile card, all information that was previously visible should return:
https://support.microsoft.com/en-us/outlook/create-view-and-edit-contacts-and-contact-lists-in-outlook
Scope of impact: Some users attempting to view contacts and Speed Dial entries in Microsoft Teams, Outlook desktop and mobile may have been impacted.
Start time: Friday, September 25, 2026, at 7:30 AM UTC
End time: Tuesday, November 24, 2026, at 10:00 AM UTC

Root cause: A problem with a contact-processing component had incorrectly separated some Profile Based Contact (PBCs) from their associated profiles when specific contact information wasn't explicitly stored, causing affected contacts to appear as blank.
Next steps:
- We're reviewing our contact-processing procedures on the affected infrastructure to help prevent this problem from happening again.
This is the final update for this event.

Scope of impact: Some users attempting to view contacts and Speed Dial entries in Microsoft Teams, Outlook desktop and mobile may be impacted. This information may be updated as our investigation continues.
